title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference: November 23, 2026
headline: Cardinals fire DC Nick Rallis and promote Terrell Austin; Carson Beck's back spasms are day-to-day, with clarity expected Wednesday.
summary: LaFleur opened by announcing the midweek change at defensive coordinator, with Terrell Austin taking over for the rest of the season. He said the decision was his alone and followed three poor weeks in which every phase fell short, including the offense. He framed the problem as collective and said execution failures fall on the coaching staff, himself first. Austin will put his own spin on the defense, and no other defensive staff changes are planned. Carson Beck was in for treatment with back spasms and is day-to-day, and the injury report on Wednesday should clarify his status. LaFleur would not commit to a quarterback and said the Washington game plan starts from the team's foundations regardless of who plays. He was complimentary of Hjalte Froholdt and the continuity he is building on the offensive line. He praised Max Melton's returns, sideline energy and gunner reps but would not say whether Melton will get defensive snaps. LaFleur also acknowledged the season is not going to the playoffs and framed the rest of it as an evaluation period for who is part of the solution.

injuries.detail: Back spasms; was in for treatment Monday. Coach called him 'minute to minute, day to day' and said more will be known Wednesday when the injury report comes out.
Missed one game (concussion per the injury report) but is listed as a full practice participant; coach praised his continued growth.

Asked whether he is on track to return after four games. Coach would not commit and said he will know more as the week goes. He tied the decision to this being the fourth week and said they would tackle the Philadelphia game next week.

signals.claim: Beck's availability will be clearer when the Wednesday injury report is released.
signals.note: Beck's back spasms make his Week status uncertain, so monitor Wednesday's report before setting QB lineups.
signals.quote: minute to minute, day to day.

signals.claim: Froholdt will continue to lead the offensive line and anchor its continuity going forward.
signals.note: A stable, improving offensive line with Froholdt leading it is mildly positive for the offense.
signals.quote: man, has he just gotten gotten better and better

signals.note: Melton showed well on returns and as a gunner, but the coach declined to say whether he will get defensive snaps.
signals.quote: I thought his energy on the sidelines with both the defense and offense was awesome.

signals.claim: Love's return timeline will become clearer later this week, with Philadelphia the next possible target.
signals.note: Love is a key skill-position player, and the coach gave no commitment on a return after the four-game mark.
signals.quote: I'll know a little bit more as this week goes.

topics.detail: Nick Rallis was let go and Terrell Austin takes over play-calling for the rest of 2026. LaFleur said it was his decision, made the morning of the press conference, and that no other defensive staff changes are being made.
LaFleur said the team is not going to the playoffs or winning a Super Bowl this year. He framed the remaining games as an opportunity to see who can be part of the solution moving forward.

He said the offense has not held up its end, citing small margins where one bad play call or execution error ends drives. He took responsibility for putting players in better positions, despite four different quarterbacks in four weeks.
He named Budda Baker and Mack Wilson as the team captains and trusted leaders who will keep the effort up.
Asked about signing players with off-field issues, he said it is handled case by case and the front office is always looking to improve the roster.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski on team preparations for Week 12 matchup vs. Vikings | Press Conference
headline: No player-specific news from Stefanski: Tommy's sideline return is undecided, a few unnamed players are being held out of today's practice, and Minnesota's heavy blitz is the main matchup concern.
summary: Stefanski used the bye week and this bonus practice day for a self-scout of both scheme and personnel. Position coaches reviewed their own areas, the run game was cut up by concept, and coordinators pulled it into a streamlined list of takeaways. He said the players will get only the key bullet points, not the full deep dive. He admitted some concepts are underused, and that the staff must decide which schemes are worth investing meeting and practice time in. He called the defense's run-stopping slide since Week 5 a product of many small issues (plan, technique, consistency) rather than one fix. He said the pass rush creates plenty of pressure but needs to turn more of it into sacks. For Minnesota, he praised Brian Flores' blitz-heavy, versatile defense and said the offense must stay on schedule and give the quarterback good answers to pressure. He added that the team is not fully into its preparation yet. On health, he said several players used the bye to get treatment, a couple will sit out today and might return Wednesday, and everything is day to day.

injuries.detail: Asked if he expects Tommy back on the sideline this week, Stefanski said he still wants to think it through and is not 100% either way.
A reporter asked about DeVante and others. Stefanski said a bunch of guys used the bye to heal, a couple will be held out today and maybe return Wednesday, and it is day to day.

topics.detail: The staff reviewed games 1-10 by concept (wide zone, duo, perimeter runs). They are deciding which schemes to keep investing in and which to streamline for consistency. Players get only the key bullet points.

Stefanski stressed staying on schedule and avoiding long down-and-distance. He also wants the quarterback to have good answers and to exploit the voids in coverage when Minnesota blitzes. A reporter said 'Mike' has struggled against pressure, and Stefanski did not address a specific player.

The team is near the top of the league in pressure rate but near the bottom in sacks. Stefanski expects sacks to come in bunches and wants to convert pressures. He gave no single reason for the run defense's decline since Week 4, only 'all of the above' and a lack of consistency.
U.S. Bank Stadium is very loud. The team will work on the silent count to handle the noise.
Stefanski praised Brian Flores' scheme and said the players are versatile and play extremely hard. He cautioned that his own preparation is not complete.

title: Jesse Minter Discusses Ravens' Defense, Marlon Humphrey's Status
headline: Ravens' defense is still inconsistent after a sixth straight loss. Marlon Humphrey's status for Sunday is open, and Lamar Jackson's situation is unclear. T.J. Tampa and Mike Green are earning more defensive snaps.
summary: Jesse Minter reviewed the Week 11 loss to Carolina, which came after Baltimore had the lead late. He admitted that calling a timeout after the fourth-down sneak would probably have been the better choice in hindsight. He said the defense is too inconsistent, with nearly every defender having 3-5 plays where he tries to do too much or misses a technique, execution or assignment. He took accountability, and when asked about giving up play-calling he said only that everything crosses his mind and he will do what he thinks is best. Marlon Humphrey is back in the building, but Minter kept their conversation private and would say only that the team will work through the week before deciding on Sunday. He praised T.J. Tampa, saying he has earned the right to be on the field, and Mike Green, who has four sacks in two games and is a bright spot. Punt return duties are undecided: LaJohntay Wester's job is under review, and Devontez Walker is a potential option. He is fine with the current quarterback room and would not speculate about Daniel Jones. On Lamar Jackson, he said only that Jackson is still in the initial part of the process and has been in the building a little.

title: Joe Brady On Preparing For The Kansas City Chiefs On A Short Week
headline: Short week vs. KC: Khalil Shakir is being asked to do more on the outside, Josh Allen's turnovers and end-of-half issues are being flagged, and Christian Benford's status will be clearer Tuesday.
summary: Brady said the Chiefs game on Thanksgiving gets the same approach as any other week. He called himself unhappy with parts of Sunday's tape and said the team's standard slipped in some phases. He described the short-week game plan as installing first and second down on Tuesday and third down that afternoon, with Monday spent on recovery work. On Josh Allen, he said the quarterback is reading coverages well but left some throws and decisions on the field. The turnovers (two on Sunday) and the poor end-of-half execution are things he wants fixed, and he partly blamed his own play calling and receiver spacing. He said Allen had no rushing attempts by chance, not by design, and he wants less reliance on QB sneaks. The run game has averaged under four yards a carry over the last five weeks. Brady attributed that to different defenses each week and to the offense being behind the chains early on Sunday, and said the team ran mostly 11 personnel. He praised Khalil Shakir and Keon Coleman as elite run blockers on the perimeter and said Shakir is being asked to do more on the outside, which lets other receivers move inside. Brady also said it was good to have Shavers back, and that he would have a better answer on Christian Benford's status the next day.

title: Brian Schottenheimer: “We’re Showing People What We’re Capable Of” | Press Conference
headline: Dak Prescott is in the best stretch Schottenheimer remembers, and the Cowboys offense is thriving after the 51-30 win. Jalen Thompson is trending toward playing Thursday at Philadelphia.
summary: Schottenheimer reviewed the 51-30 win over Tennessee and called the offense's plan and execution strong. He said the team's inconsistency comes down to execution, and that doing simple things better, especially tackling, helped the defense. He liked the pass rush and the containment of the quarterback, but pointed to a late pass interference penalty on Caleb Downs and a Hail Mary play where a defender failed to tag a player down. The big theme was Dak Prescott, whose command and confidence he called the best of any stretch he can remember. Javonte Williams, Jashaun Corbin (pass protection), George Pickens (yards after the catch), James Houston (rotation) and DeMarvion Overshown (versatile alignments) all got praise. He said Mike Pettine's first week as defensive play caller went well, with Christian Parker working alongside him on the sideline. On injuries, he was very optimistic about Jalen Thompson playing on the short week, and Prescott's hand is fine. Dallas now turns to the Eagles on Thanksgiving, and he expects Philadelphia's quarterback to spread the ball around and try to get Saquon going.

title: HC Sean Payton following Denver’s Week 11 win: ‘We’re still finding the little things to improve’
headline: Jonah Coleman ran for 100+ yards and 3 TDs in Denver's win, and Sean Payton praised the line's blocking and his contact running. Evan Engram also got a pointed shout-out.

He called the win good but said it felt like two games: Denver built an early lead, the Raiders fought back, and the same thing happened in the second half. He credited Ja'Quan McMillian's instincts and ball skills on a big play, and said the Raiders looked much different from what Denver is used to seeing. Offensively he credited the front for blocking well for Jonah Coleman, who he said runs with good balance and contact. He said Matt Peart's time at left guard was about giving Peart work, and that Ben Powers remains very important to the offense. He liked Evan Engram's yards after the catch on a key third-down conversion but said it is hard to predict when targets will go his way. He also said he doesn't regret the 4th-and-half-yard sneak call, that he had a better play for the late fourth down, and that he never considered a 67-yard field goal over a Hail Mary at the half. title: Liam Coen on Areas to Improve Entering Week 12 | Press Conference
headline: Bhayshul Tuten re-aggravated his ankle, may be limited all week and could be rested; Ameer Abdullah is the new punt returner and Wyatt Milum filled in at left tackle.
summary: Coen opened by saying the loss in New York was on both sides: the Jaguars were beaten and also beat themselves. Coen said Walker Little and Jerry Jones (likely Jarrian Jones) have no short-term concerns, and Wyatt Milum came in at left tackle without flinching. title: Liam Coen Recaps Loss to Giants in Week 11 | Press Conference
headline: Coen blames himself for a sloppy 23-18 loss to the Giants: red zone play-calling, a failed fourth-and-1 pass, and a new center. Josh Cameron was open on that play, and Coen says he'll run the ball more in the red zone.
summary: Coen opened by saying the team was not prepared well enough and put that directly on himself. He pointed to 13 penalties to the Giants' six, many of them pre-snap, and tied some to a new center in the lineup (Jonah Monheim) and trying to anticipate silent counts on the road against strong pass rushers. He called his red zone plan a mistake: after calling bad runs the previous week at Tennessee, he leaned pass-heavy and now says they should have run more. The offense went 1-for-6 in the red zone, and he said the run game was ineffective early, which put them in second-and-long and third-and-long. On the late fourth-and-1 from the 11, he said Jacksonville had the right look but missed the read to Josh Cameron, who was open. Coen explained that the earlier decision to kick a field goal while trailing was driven by the analytics charts, which favored kicking and getting a stop. He said Trevor Lawrence competed hard and gave them a chance, though Lawrence threw a number of 50-50 balls, partly because of pressure, with Parker Washington on the receiving end of a few. Coen said the defense didn't play great early but held the Giants to 23 points, and that the team lacked complementary football and special teams play, concluding they were outplayed and outcoached.

title: Head Coach Jim Harbaugh Postgame Press Conference vs. Jets
headline: Chargers fall one field goal short to the Jets; Harbaugh gives no injury or role news, but says the offense ran well, was efficient on third down, and needs faster tempo on the final drive.

Defensively, the deep ball was handled well, but the run defense and third-down penalties that gave up two touchdowns need fixing. On special teams, he said Kene Nwangwu was close to breaking a return and that someone named Isaiah stepped in well as returner.

title: HC Aaron Glenn Postgame Press Conference (11/22) | Week 11
headline: Jets snap their losing streak with a balanced offense, Sterling Shepard's TD and Geno Smith's strong play; no new injuries and Geno's ankle is expected to be managed for next week.
summary: Aaron Glenn opened by saying the Jets got a win and came out of it with no injuries. He was pleased with the offense: the run game worked, the team was good in the red zone and on third down, and offensive coordinator Frank got credit for a strong game. Glenn said Frank called plays from the sideline this week, a change the two discussed earlier in the week, and that he wants to keep it because it worked. He conceded the defense still has to clean up third-down penalties. He called Sterling Shepard an 'Energizer bunny' who stays ready despite being inactive in recent weeks, and praised Geno Smith's comeback season, his preparation and his leadership. David Bailey drew high praise as a pressure player with close to ten sacks and several forced fumbles. Geno played through an ankle issue on adrenaline, and Glenn expects him to be sore but manageable for next week. Glenn also liked the balanced game plan in which eight different players caught passes and both Braelon Allen and Breece Hall had good games. He described next week as a holiday-week game.

injuries.detail: Played through an ankle injury; Glenn expects him to be a little sore but says the team will manage it and have him ready for next week.

signals.note: Shepard scored the touchdown that broke the team's TD drought after being inactive for weeks, but there is no stated plan for a bigger role.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: November 23, 2026
headline: Joe Milton III earned the coach's trust after his best game, Jonathan Jones got the hot-hand snaps over Riq Woolen at CB, and Eli Stowers still has no offensive role heading into Thursday's game against Dallas.
summary: Sirianni opened by praising Joe Milton III's rapid growth. He pointed to Milton's ability to play the next play regardless of what just happened, plus his constant work in the building, and said Milton is coming off his best performance. He praised Quinyon Mitchell for holding DK Metcalf to almost nothing and called him a quiet but fiercely competitive player. He said Mitchell will face another tough test on Thursday against a Cowboys offense with three good receivers. He credited Jeremiah Trotter Jr. for football IQ, toughness and special teams background, and shared the credit for the linebackers' big day with the defensive line's block destruction and with Jihaad Campbell. On Eli Stowers' lack of offensive snaps, he said the game flow dictated the personnel, but the intention is to get him involved. He declined to engage on a possible Daniel Jones addition, said the team likes its QB room, and called Tanner McKee very capable. At corner, Jonathan Jones was supposed to be mixed in with Riq Woolen, but he played well and the staff rode the hot hand. Sirianni said he will talk through that with his players and that everyone is needed against Dallas. Finally, he described his short-week approach as committing to a process and reviewing it afterward.

signals.claim: Milton keeps developing and is trusted to close out games; coming off his best performance.
signals.note: The coach is openly confident in Milton, and the team is not looking at outside QB options.

signals.claim: Trotter continues to improve as the middle linebacker and had a standout game.

The linebackers' big day was helped by good block destruction from the defensive front, and the coach credited the whole defense.

title: WATCH: The Mike McCarthy Press Conference Show presented by PNC (Week 12)
headline: McCarthy says DK Metcalf talks went well, with no league discipline known. Michael Pittman is expected back, Alex Highsmith is unlikely for Friday vs DEN, and the offense plans to run more.
summary: After back-to-back losses, McCarthy spent much of the session on DK Metcalf's ejection against Philadelphia. He called their one-on-one conversation productive and said Metcalf was accountable. He is not aware of any league discipline and would keep any internal discipline private. He said he believes in second chances. On the offense, he admitted the unit hasn't played well in two weeks, said he starts with himself, and said the run game needs more attempts. He kept Aaron Rodgers as the quarterback and brushed aside a question about using other quarterbacks. He praised Roman Wilson and Max Hurleman for giving the offense a lift and said he is very confident Michael Pittman will be out there this week. On defense, he said it will be tough for Alex Highsmith to play Friday against Denver, and Nick Herbig is only in the rehab group. title: Shanahan Reflects on Win Over Vikings, Reaches 100 Combined Victories
headline: 49ers beat the Vikings' elite defense in Mexico City. Purdy, Kittle, Evans and Keenan Allen all got praise, but RT Colton McKivitz is likely out for the year with a broken, dislocated ankle.
summary: Shanahan was happy with the win in Mexico City, where the crowd gave the 49ers a true home-field advantage. He called Brock Purdy unbelievable against a Vikings defense that stuffed runs and took away throws, and said Purdy let it rip without hesitating and protected the ball. Purdy got the game ball, though Shanahan said everyone deserved one. He singled out George Kittle (an explosive touchdown from 17 yards out, a drawn holding penalty, and big early catches) and Mike Evans, who has been battling to get back. He also praised Keenan Allen's target volume over the last two weeks. The injury news was bad: Colton McKivitz left with an ankle injury that they think is broken and dislocated, which Shanahan compared to Fred Warner's injury last year. A backup stepped up in his place and Shanahan expects him to keep starting. A player Shanahan called Demo, most likely Deommodore Lenoir, also left with a foot injury. Shanahan said targets got spread around because players rotated heavily in the altitude, and that he doesn't distribute the ball just to be friendly. The team gets Monday and Tuesday off and returns Wednesday, and Shanahan noted the next opponent is coming off a bye.

title: Todd Bowles on Path Forward: ‘It Starts With Us’ | Press Conference
headline: Bucs CBs Jacob Parrish and Benjamin Morrison both got MRIs after the Lions game, so the secondary is thin heading into Monday night against Carolina. Baker Mayfield seems to have come out of his foot issue okay.
summary: Bowles said Jacob Parrish and Benjamin Morrison both left the Lions game hurt and are getting MRIs, with an update expected later in the day. Losing both forced the team to play its third corner and rearrange the secondary, but Bowles made no excuses. He named Ayden Garnes as a possible replacement, saying Garnes has practiced well, and he is also watching how close Josh Williams is to returning. He was noncommittal about moving Keionte Scott outside, saying that would put a lot on his plate. Elijah Roberts is in concussion protocol, and Bowles said he has no other injury concerns. On offense, Bowles said the team changed things in the passing game after the bye and still needs to be better there. He said they had well-designed plays they failed to execute, and that two delay-of-game penalties came from a combination of slow huddles, slow line approaches and slow play calls. He said David Walker played only 19 snaps because the Lions' run-heavy personnel called for bigger bodies, but that Walker is a big part of the plan and his snaps should grow as he learns the system. Bowles said the team needs to score more points and finish games by minimizing mistakes and winning field position. He called Vita Vea's frustration an isolated incident. He also said Mayfield probably came out of the game fine with some soreness, though he showed some rust. Next up is a division game against the Panthers on Monday night.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Saleh says Tyjae Spears was shut down to protect his knee, and Nicholas Singleton has a chance to play in the last seven games. No timeline was given, and the defense is still struggling.
summary: Saleh opened by saying the team is still evaluating the players hurt in yesterday's game and will share the injury list on Wednesday. He blamed the defense's poor showing on execution of technique and lost one-on-one matchups, not effort, and said coaches also need to give players better leverage. He thought the offense moved the ball well, with Cam Ward's production mostly not garbage time. The offense got three field goals and left some touchdowns on the field, and penalties hurt early drives. He credited Dak Prescott for playing at a very high level and said the defense failed whether it rushed four or blitzed. He noted that Jacksonville is coming up again, after three strong offenses in consecutive weeks. He defended the trades of Jeffery Simmons and Amani Hooker as expected, said ownership support is total, and said players and coaches who don't improve will not stay. On Tyjae Spears, he praised the young man for playing through a knee at about 70% and said the team had to protect him from himself so he can get the knee fixed. Asked about Nick Singleton, he said there is a chance he plays in the last seven games but gave no timeframe.

The Simmons and Hooker trades were expected to hurt the defense, and Saleh said ownership is fully supportive. He said players and coaches who do not improve will not stay, and the final seven games will shape roster decisions.
